project.title: Pax6os1 pull-down in MIN6 cell lysate
project.projectDescription: Pull-down experiment to identify protein binding partners of the lncRNA Pax6os1 in mouse insulinoma cell line MIN6 using in-vitro transcribed RNA.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: The bait RNA (Pax6os1 or 3' UTR from Slc16a1 as control) was in vitro transcribed together with a tRNA-stabilised streptavidin-binding aptamer. The generated RNA were used in a protein binding assay with streptavidin beads (Sigma, S1638). A volume of 50 µl of beads was washed three times in 250 µl 1X Aptamer buffer (20 mM Hepes, 150 mM NaCl,10 mM MgCl2, 0.5% (v/v) Triton X100, pH 7.02) using centrifugation at 800 xg for one min. The RNA input was prepared using 100 µg RNA, 1 U/µl RiboLock RNase inhibitor (ThermoFisher), and 1X Complete Proteinase inhibitor (Roche), in 1X Aptamer buffer. Rotating incubation of the RNA input and beads was performed at 4oC for 4 h. Post-incubation, beads were washed again three times in 250 µl 1X Aptamer buffer before being inoculated with the protein input. To enable later proteomic analysis between the control and the Pax6os1 samples, two different SILAC MIN6 lysates were used, with Pax6os1 and Slc16a1 corresponding to the heavy and light labelled lysates respectively. The protein MIN6 lysate (4 mg) was prepared by addition of Avidin (10 µg/mg protein)(Pierce, 21121) and Yeast RNA (0.5 mg/mg protein) (Sigma, R6760) and incubated at 4oC for 20 min. before centrifuging at 24,100 xg. The supernatant fraction was collected and supplemented with 1 U/µl RiboLock RNase inhibitor prior to being added to the beads and incubated at 4oC overnight under rotation. The next day the protein lysate was removed and the beads washed three times in 250 µl 1X Aptamer buffer. An additional wash in 1X High salt aptamer buffer (20 mM Hepes, 400 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl2, 0.5% (v/v) Triton X100) was performed to minimize unspecific protein binding. The streptavidin aptamer and bound complex were eluted from the beads using 50 µl of 10 mM Biotin (pH 7.2) (Sigma, B4501) suspended in the 1X Aptamer buffer. The final elute was stored at -20oC.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Mass spectrometry was performed by the Proteomics Facility, at The University of Bristol (URL:https://www.bristol.ac.uk/life-sciences/research/facilities/proteomics/) in collaboration with Dr Kate Heesom. In brief, the SILAC samples were pooled and three slices obtained on an SDS-PAGE gel. The slices were digested (DigestPro automated digestion unit (Intavis Ltd.)) and peptides fractionated (Ultimate 3000 nano-LC system). Peptides were injected into an Acclaim PepMap C18 nano-trap column (Thermo Scientific) in 1% (v/v) formic acid, washed with 0.5% (v/v) acetonitrile and resolved on a 250 mm × 75 μm Acclaim PepMap C18 reverse phase analytical column (Thermo Scientific) over a 150 min. organic gradient with a flow rate of 300 nl min-1. Ionization of the peptides was performed with nano-electrospray ionization at 2.0 kV using a stainless-steel emitter with an internal diameter of 30 μm (Thermo Scientific) and a capillary temperature of 275°C. An Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid mass spectrometer controlled by Xcalibur 3.0 software (Thermo Scientific) was used for spectra acquisition. Proteome Discoverer software v2.1 (Thermo Scientific) was used for raw data processing, searched against the UniProt Mus musculus database (downloaded November 2018; 81925 sequences) using the SEQUEST algorithm.
